summary: Rust and Swift clients preserve outer action-application metadata and classify conflicting or malformed certainty conservatively; Rust exposes a matching completed-receipt predicate and typed, prepared-request submission for explicit recovery.

replay.detail: No stored format changes. Explicit retries still retain the original request identity, key, fence and transport; a later refusal does not establish that an earlier ambiguous attempt was unapplied.

schema.detail: Reads the already-declared optional outer applied field alongside legacy details.applied. Missing and explicit null remain distinct and raw values round-trip.

rules.detail: No server action or authority rule changes. Unknown or malformed present metadata dominates a none value or stale/rate shortcut. Completion requires action-result kind, Completed status and the original action ID.

compatibility.detail: Older error envelopes remain readable. Rust ErrorEnvelope gains a public applied field, so external struct literals must add applied: None when no outer value exists. Swift's existing internal initializer keeps its defaulted call shape. Rust adds submit_action for an existing typed ActionRequest and prepare_message_send to sign and capture a message once; the normal message_send convenience method delegates to that preparation path. Explicit null and malformed metadata are retained rather than treated as a guarantee of nonapplication.

downtime.detail: No downtime or server migration required.

manual.detail: Regenerate clients from the owning templates; no runtime configuration is required.

recovery.detail: Callers can preserve uncertain original submissions instead of unlocking new writes after contradictory or malformed error metadata. These helpers do not prove delivery after an earlier uncertain attempt.
